#### Factor effects
The code below extracts and plots the factor effects for the combined model. A point is shown for the effect of each model but error bars are shown only for Model 1. 

```{r Factor effects lot models, eval=TRUE, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, results = 'hide', fig.width=20, fig.height=20}

factor_variables <- c(house_type = "House type",
                      municipality_type = "Municipality type",
                      type = "Type",
                      roof_type = "Roof type",
                      wall_type = "Wall type",
                      heating_type = "Heating type")

make_termwise_df <- function(model, model_data, variable, interaction_by = "municipality_type") {

  v_vals <- unique(model_data[[variable]])
  
  if (is.null(interaction_by)) {
    df <- data.frame(setNames(list(v_vals), variable), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  } else {
    m_vals <- unique(model_data[[interaction_by]])
    grid_list <- setNames(list(v_vals, m_vals), c(variable, interaction_by))
    df <- expand.grid(grid_list, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    df[[interaction_by]] <- factor(df[[interaction_by]], 
                                   levels = levels(model_data[[interaction_by]]))
  }
  for (var in setdiff(all.vars(formula(model)), names(df))) {
    x <- model_data[[var]]
    if (is.factor(x)) {
      df[[var]] <- factor(rep(levels(x)[1], nrow(df)), levels = levels(x))
    } else {
      df[[var]] <- 0
    }
  }
  return(df)
}

combine_all_term_effects <- function(df, term, interaction_by = "municipality_type") {
  pattern <- paste0("^", term, "$|^", term, ":" ,"|:", term, "$")
  cols_to_sum <- grep(pattern, names(df), value = TRUE)
  df[[paste0("effect_", term)]] <- rowSums(as.matrix(df[cols_to_sum]))
  return(df)
}

combine_all_term_se <- function(df, term, interaction_by = "municipality_type") {
  pattern <- paste0("^", term, "$|^", term, ":" ,"|:", term, "$")
  cols_to_sum <- grep(pattern, names(df), value = TRUE)
  df[[paste0("se_", term)]] <- sqrt(rowSums(as.matrix(df[cols_to_sum])^2))
  return(df)
}

plot_term_effect <- function(df, term, interaction_by = "municipality_type") {
  
  effect_col <- paste0("effect_", term)
  lower_col <- paste0("lower_", effect_col)
  upper_col <- paste0("upper_", effect_col)
  df_sub <- df %>% filter(term == !!term)
  plot_title <- paste("Partial effect of", gsub("_", " ", term))

  p <- ggplot(df_sub, aes(x = .data[[term]], 
                          y = .data[[effect_col]], 
                          shape = Model,
                          group = interaction(Model, if (identical(term, interaction_by) || 
                                                        !(interaction_by %in% names(df_sub))) NULL 
                                                     else .data[[interaction_by]]))) +
      geom_pointrange(data = subset(df_sub, Model == "Model 1"),
                      aes(ymin = .data[[lower_col]], ymax = .data[[upper_col]]),
                      position = position_dodge(width = 0.5),
                      size = 0.8) +
      geom_point(data = subset(df_sub, Model != "Model 1"),
                 position = position_dodge(width = 0.5),
                 size = 2.5) +
      coord_flip() +
      labs(x = NULL, y = "Partial effect", title = plot_title, shape = "Model") +
      theme(axis.text.y = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

  if (interaction_by %in% names(df_sub)) {
      color_var <- if (term == interaction_by) term else interaction_by
      p <- p + aes(color = .data[[color_var]]) +
      scale_color_brewer(palette = "Dark2", name = "Municipality type")
  }

  return(p)
}

factor_dfs <- list()

for (model_name in names(models_combined)) {

  model <- models_combined[[model_name]]
  model_data <- model.frame(model)
  relevant_factors <- factor_variables[names(factor_variables) %in% all.vars(formula(model))]

  for (var in names(relevant_factors)) {

    interaction <- if (var == "municipality_type") NULL else "municipality_type"
    df <- make_termwise_df(model, model_data, var, interaction_by = interaction)
    df$term <- var

    terms <- predict.gam(model, df, type = "terms", se.fit = TRUE)
    df_predictions <- as.data.frame(terms$fit)
    df_se <- as.data.frame(terms$se.fit)

    combined_predictions <- combine_all_term_effects(df_predictions, var, interaction_by = interaction) %>% 
                            select(starts_with("effect_"))
    
    combined_se <- combine_all_term_se(df_se, var, interaction_by = interaction) %>% 
                   select(starts_with("se_"))

    df_final <- df %>% select(all_of(c(var, interaction)), term) %>%
                       bind_cols(combined_predictions) %>%
                       bind_cols(combined_se) %>%
                       mutate(across(starts_with("effect_"),
                                     ~ . - 1.96 * get(str_replace(cur_column(), 
                                     "effect_", 
                                     "se_")),
                                     .names = "lower_{.col}")) %>%
                       mutate(across(starts_with("effect_"),
                                     ~ . + 1.96 * get(str_replace(cur_column(), "effect_", "se_")),
                                     .names = "upper_{.col}"))

    df_final$Model <- sub("^Model", "Model ", model_name)
    factor_dfs[[length(factor_dfs) + 1]] <- df_final
  }
}

df_all_factors <- bind_rows(factor_dfs)
plot_factors <- lapply(names(factor_variables), function(term) {plot_term_effect(df_all_factors, term)})
names(plot_factors) <- names(factor_variables)

wrap_plots(plot_factors, ncol = 2) +
           plot_layout(guides = "collect") &
           theme(legend.position = "bottom",
                 legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
                 legend.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
                 legend.box = "horizontal",
                 legend.justification = "center")

```

## 4.4 Predictive performance
The code below extracts various residual types for each type of lot model and calculates different performance measures for the training and validation set. Note that using N-fold cross-validation means that there are N-1 estimates for each training point, and the training error is simply taken as the average over these. 

```{r Performance lot sales, eval=TRUE, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE}

# -------------------------
# 1. Residuals for lot-sales evaluation
# -------------------------

get_lot_residuals <- function(models, dataset_lot_sales_cv, model_approach,
                              fold_from_name = TRUE) {
  
  residual_list <- future_lapply(seq_along(models), function(i) {
    
    model_name <- names(models)[i]
    model <- models[[i]]
    
    fold <- if (fold_from_name) {
      as.integer(sub("^Model(\\d+).*$", "\\1", model_name))
    } else {
      i
    }
    
    predicted_sales_price <- as.vector(predict.gam(model, newdata = dataset_lot_sales_cv, type = "response"))
    
    tibble(model_approach = model_approach,
           Model = model_name,
           sales_price = dataset_lot_sales_cv$sales_price,
           sales_date_numeric = dataset_lot_sales_cv$sales_date_numeric,
           predicted_sales_price = predicted_sales_price,
           residual_sales_price = predicted_sales_price - dataset_lot_sales_cv$sales_price,
           residual_sales_price_percent = (predicted_sales_price - dataset_lot_sales_cv$sales_price) / dataset_lot_sales_cv$sales_price * 100,
           residual_sales_price_log = log(predicted_sales_price) - log(dataset_lot_sales_cv$sales_price),
           ratio = predicted_sales_price / dataset_lot_sales_cv$sales_price,
           validation = dataset_lot_sales_cv$validation_set == fold,
           id = dataset_lot_sales_cv$id,
           municipality_type = dataset_lot_sales_cv$municipality_type)
  })
  
  bind_rows(residual_list)
}

# -------------------------
# 2. Residuals for each approach
# -------------------------

residual_direct_lot <- get_lot_residuals(models = models_direct,
                                         dataset_lot_sales_cv = dataset_lot_sales_cv_standardized,
                                         model_approach = "Direct lot model")

residual_standard_property <- get_lot_residuals(models = models_standard_property,
                                                dataset_lot_sales_cv = dataset_lot_sales_cv_standardized,
                                                model_approach = "Standard property model")

residual_combined <- get_lot_residuals(models = models_combined,
                                       dataset_lot_sales_cv = dataset_lot_sales_cv_standardized,
                                       model_approach = "Combined model")

residual_df_lot_models <- bind_rows(residual_direct_lot,
                                    residual_standard_property,
                                    residual_combined)

saveRDS(residual_df_lot_models, "saved_files/residual_df_lot_models.rds")


# -------------------------
# 3. Performance helper
# -------------------------

summarise_lot_performance <- function(residual_df, group_vars) {
  
  residual_df %>% mutate(dataset_type = if_else(validation, "Validation", "Training")) %>%
                  group_by(across(all_of(group_vars))) %>%
                  summarise(MALE = mean(abs(residual_sales_price_log), na.rm = TRUE),
                            MAPE = mean(abs(residual_sales_price_percent), na.rm = TRUE),
                            MAE = mean(abs(residual_sales_price), na.rm = TRUE),
                            PM20 = mean(abs(residual_sales_price_percent) <= 20, na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
                            COD = mean(abs(ratio - median(ratio, na.rm = TRUE)), na.rm = TRUE) / median(ratio, na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
                            PRD = mean(ratio, na.rm = TRUE) /(sum(predicted_sales_price, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(sales_price, na.rm = TRUE)),
                            .groups = "drop")
}

# -------------------------
# 4. Countrywide and municipality-type performance
# -------------------------

performance_countrywide_lot_models <- summarise_lot_performance(residual_df_lot_models, group_vars = c("model_approach", "dataset_type")) %>%
                                      mutate(municipality_type = "Countrywide")

performance_municipality_type_lot_models <- summarise_lot_performance(residual_df_lot_models, group_vars = c("model_approach", "dataset_type", "municipality_type")) %>%
                                            mutate(PRD = NA_real_)

performance_lot_models <- bind_rows(performance_countrywide_lot_models, performance_municipality_type_lot_models)

municipality_levels <- c("Countrywide", sort(setdiff(unique(performance_lot_models$municipality_type), "Countrywide")))

performance_sorted_lot_models <- performance_lot_models %>%
                                 mutate(model_approach = factor(model_approach, levels = c("Direct lot model", "Standard property model", "Combined model")),
                                        dataset_type = factor(dataset_type, levels = c("Training", "Validation")),
                                        municipality_type = factor(municipality_type, levels = municipality_levels),
                                        MAE = round(MAE, 0),
                                        PRD = ifelse(is.na(PRD), "", round(PRD, 2))) %>%
                                 arrange(model_approach, municipality_type, dataset_type) %>%
                                 rename(Approach = model_approach,
                                        Type = dataset_type,
                                        `Municipality type` = municipality_type,
                                        `MAPE [%]` = MAPE,
                                        `MAE [DKK]` = MAE,
                                        `PM20 [%]` = PM20,
                                        `COD [%]` = COD)
       
saveRDS(performance_sorted_lot_models, "saved_files/performance_sorted_lot_models.rds")
```

## 4.5 Prediction stability
The code below evaluates the stability of predicted lot values across the fold-specific models for each of the three modelling approaches. All models within an ensemble are used to predict lot values for the same set of properties on the link scale. For each property, the mean prediction and the standard deviation across the fold-specific predictions are calculated. The standard deviation across the model ensembles is used as a measure of sensitivity to perturbations of the training data.

```{r Stability lot models, eval=TRUE, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE}

# -------------------------
# 1. Settings
# -------------------------

cap <- 0.2

model_sets <- list("Direct lot model" = models_direct,
                   "Standard property model" = models_standard_property,
                   "Combined model" = models_combined)

# -------------------------
# 2. Prepare prediction datasets
# -------------------------

dataset_properties_combined_lot <- dataset_properties_standardized %>% 
                                   mutate(type = factor("Lot sale", levels = c("Lot sale", "Property sale")),
                                          type_ordered = ordered("Lot sale", levels = c("Lot sale", "Property sale")))

prediction_datasets <- list("Direct lot model" = dataset_properties,
                            "Standard property model" = dataset_properties,
                            "Combined model" = dataset_properties_combined_lot)

# -------------------------
# 3. Ensemble spread function
# -------------------------

spread_model_set <- function(model_set, dataset) {
  
  predictions <- imap(model_set, function(model, fold_name) {
    
    preds <- predict.gam(model,
                         newdata = dataset,
                         type = "link")
    
    tibble(!!paste0("pred_", fold_name) := as.vector(preds))
    
  })
  
  pred_matrix <- bind_cols(predictions)
  pred_mat <- as.matrix(pred_matrix)
  
  bind_cols(dataset, pred_matrix) %>%
  mutate(mean_Ensemble = rowMeans(pred_mat, na.rm = TRUE),
         sigma_Ensemble = apply(pred_mat, 1, sd, na.rm = TRUE))
}

# -------------------------
# 4. Predict for all three approaches
# -------------------------

if (load) {
  
  dataset_spread <- readRDS("saved_files/dataset_spread.rds")
  
} else {
  
  dataset_spread <- imap(
    model_sets,
    function(model_set, model_approach) {
      
      message("Predicting ensemble spread for ", model_approach, " ...")
      
      spread_model_set(model_set = model_set, dataset = prediction_datasets[[model_approach]])
      
    }
  )
  
  saveRDS(dataset_spread, "saved_files/dataset_spread.rds")
}

# -------------------------
# 5. Long-format spread data
# -------------------------

spread_long <- imap_dfr(
  dataset_spread,
  function(df, model_approach) {
    
    df %>% transmute(model_approach = model_approach, sigma_Ensemble = sigma_Ensemble)
    
  }
)

saveRDS(spread_long, "saved_files/spread_long.rds")

# -------------------------
# 6. Summary table
# -------------------------

spread_summary <- spread_long %>%
                  group_by(model_approach) %>%
                  summarise(mean_sigma = mean(sigma_Ensemble, na.rm = TRUE),
                            median_sigma = median(sigma_Ensemble, na.rm = TRUE),
                            p75_sigma = quantile(sigma_Ensemble, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
                            p90_sigma = quantile(sigma_Ensemble, 0.90, na.rm = TRUE),
                            p95_sigma = quantile(sigma_Ensemble, 0.95, na.rm = TRUE),
                            .groups = "drop")

saveRDS(spread_summary, "saved_files/spread_summary.rds")

# -------------------------
# 7. Density plot: all models in one plot
# -------------------------

plot_ensemble_density <- ggplot(filter(spread_long, sigma_Ensemble < 1.0),
                                aes(x = sigma_Ensemble,
                                    color = model_approach,
                                    fill = model_approach)) +
                         geom_density(alpha = 0.15,
                                      linewidth = 0.8,
                                      na.rm = TRUE) +
                         coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, cap)) +
                         labs(title = "Ensemble spread across lot-value approaches",
                              x = "Ensemble spread (link scale)",
                              y = "Density",
                              color = NULL,
                              fill = NULL) +
                         theme_minimal() +
                         theme(legend.position = c(0.7, 0.75))

saveRDS(plot_ensemble_density, "saved_files/plot_ensemble_density.rds")
print(plot_ensemble_density)

# -------------------------
# 8. Base map
# -------------------------

base_map <- ggplot() +
            geom_contour(data = coordinate_grid,
                         aes(x = coordinate_east,
                             y = coordinate_north,
                             z = as.numeric(!ocean)),
                         color = "black",
                         linewidth = 0.1) +
            coord_fixed() +
            theme_void(base_size = 10)

# -------------------------
# 9. Geographic uncertainty plots
# -------------------------

plot_ensemble_geographic <- imap(
  dataset_spread,
  function(df, model_approach) {
    
    base_map +
    geom_point(data = df,
               aes(x = coordinate_east,
                   y = coordinate_north,
                   color = sigma_Ensemble),
               size = 0.2) +
    scale_color_viridis_c(option = "plasma",
                          name = "Ensemble uncertainty",
                          limits = c(0, cap),
                          oob = squish) +
    labs(title = paste(model_approach, "- Ensemble uncertainty")) +
    theme(legend.position = c(0.7, 0.75), 
          legend.box = "horizontal")
  }
)

saveRDS(plot_ensemble_geographic, "saved_files/plot_ensemble_geographic.rds")
wrap_plots(plot_ensemble_geographic, ncol = 2)
```

## 4.6 Property-lot-building decomposition
The code below decomposes predicted property values into estimated lot and building components for each modelling approach and cross-validation fold. For the direct and standard-property approaches, property values are taken from the previously fitted property models, while lot values are predicted using the corresponding lot model. For the combined approach, property, standardized-property, and lot values are generated from the same joint model by changing the sale type and building characteristics supplied at prediction.

Building value is defined as the difference between the predicted property value and predicted lot value. The same decomposition is also calculated for the standardized property. The resulting values are summarized using measures of central tendency, dispersion, selected quantiles, building shares, values per square metre, and the frequency of negative building-value estimates.

```{r Property, building and lot values, eval=TRUE, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE}

# -------------------------
# Property, lot and building value decomposition
# -------------------------

# -------------------------
# Settings
# -------------------------

x_limits <- c(-2, 15)
density_adjust <- 1.5

building_value_limits <- c(-2, 8)
living_space_limits <- c(0, 400)
year_built_limits <- c(1900, 2024)

model_sets <- list(direct_lot_model = models_direct,
                   standard_property_model = models_standard_property,
                   combined_model = models_combined)

# -------------------------
# Helpers
# -------------------------

prepare_type <- function(data, type_value) {
  
  data %>% mutate(type = factor(type_value, levels = c("Lot sale", "Property sale")),
                  type_ordered = ordered(type, levels = c("Lot sale", "Property sale")))
}

get_property_value_vars <- function(fold_name) {
  
  property_model <- str_extract(fold_name, "Model\\d+")
  stopifnot(!is.na(property_model))
  
  list(property_value_var = paste0("property_value_", property_model),
       standard_property_value_var = paste0("standard_property_value_", property_model))
  
}

decompose_models <- function(model_set,
                             dataset_properties,
                             dataset_properties_standardized,
                             combined = FALSE) {
  
  imap(model_set, function(model, fold_name) {
    
    if (combined) {
      
      lot_value <- predict.gam(model,
                               newdata = prepare_type(dataset_properties_standardized, "Lot sale"),
                               type = "response") %>% 
                   as.vector()
      
      property_value <- predict.gam(model,
                                    newdata = prepare_type(dataset_properties, "Property sale"),
                                    type = "response") %>% 
                        as.vector()
      
      standard_property_value <- predict.gam(model,
                                             newdata = prepare_type(dataset_properties_standardized, "Property sale"),
                                             type = "response") %>% 
                                 as.vector()
      
    } else {
      
      vars <- get_property_value_vars(fold_name)
      
      lot_value <- predict.gam(model,
                               newdata = dataset_properties,
                               type = "response") %>% 
                   as.vector()
      
      property_value <- dataset_properties[[vars$property_value_var]]
      standard_property_value <- dataset_properties[[vars$standard_property_value_var]]
      
    }
    
    building_value <- property_value - lot_value
    standard_building_value <- standard_property_value - lot_value
    
    tibble(id = dataset_properties$id,
           property_value = property_value,
           standard_property_value = standard_property_value,
           lot_value = lot_value,
           building_value = building_value,
           standard_building_value = standard_building_value,
           building_share = building_value / property_value,
           standard_building_share = standard_building_value / standard_property_value,
           building_value_per_m2 = building_value / dataset_properties$living_space,
           standard_building_value_per_m2 = standard_building_value / 140,
           living_space = dataset_properties$living_space,
           year_built = dataset_properties$year_built)
    
  })
}


summarise_value <- function(x, prefix) {
  
  tibble(!!paste0(prefix, "_mean") := mean(x, na.rm = TRUE),
         !!paste0(prefix, "_median") := median(x, na.rm = TRUE),
         !!paste0(prefix, "_sd") := sd(x, na.rm = TRUE),
         !!paste0(prefix, "_mad") := mad(x, na.rm = TRUE),
         !!paste0(prefix, "_iqr") := IQR(x, na.rm = TRUE),
         !!paste0(prefix, "_q05") := quantile(x, 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
         !!paste0(prefix, "_q10") := quantile(x, 0.10, na.rm = TRUE),
         !!paste0(prefix, "_q25") := quantile(x, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
         !!paste0(prefix, "_q75") := quantile(x, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
         !!paste0(prefix, "_q90") := quantile(x, 0.90, na.rm = TRUE),
         !!paste0(prefix, "_q95") := quantile(x, 0.95, na.rm = TRUE),
         !!paste0(prefix, "_min") := min(x, na.rm = TRUE),
         !!paste0(prefix, "_max") := max(x, na.rm = TRUE),
         !!paste0(prefix, "_n_negative") := sum(x < 0, na.rm = TRUE),
         !!paste0(prefix, "_share_negative") := mean(x < 0, na.rm = TRUE) * 100)
}

summarise_decomposition <- function(df) {
  
  bind_cols(tibble(n = nrow(df)),
            summarise_value(df$property_value, "property_value"),
            summarise_value(df$standard_property_value, "standard_property_value"),
            summarise_value(df$lot_value, "lot_value"),
            summarise_value(df$building_value, "building_value"),
            summarise_value(df$standard_building_value, "standard_building_value"),
            summarise_value(df$building_share, "building_share"),
            summarise_value(df$standard_building_share, "standard_building_share"),
            summarise_value(df$building_value_per_m2, "building_value_per_m2"),
            summarise_value(df$standard_building_value_per_m2, "standard_building_value_per_m2"))
}

density_layer <- function(df, var, label) {
  
  df_layer <- df %>%
              transmute(value = .data[[var]] / 1e6) %>%
              filter(is.finite(value),
                     value >= x_limits[1],
                     value <= x_limits[2])
  
  geom_density(data = df_layer,
               mapping = aes(x = value, color = label, fill = label),
               alpha = 0.3,
               linewidth = 0.8,
               adjust = density_adjust,
               na.rm = TRUE)
}

make_density_plot <- function(df, model_approach, fold_name) {
  
  ggplot() + density_layer(df, "property_value", "Property value") +
             density_layer(df, "standard_property_value", "Standard property value") +
             density_layer(df, "lot_value", "Lot value") +
             density_layer(df, "building_value", "Building value") +
             density_layer(df, "standard_building_value", "Standard building value") +
             coord_cartesian(xlim = x_limits) +

             labs(title = paste(model_approach, "-", fold_name),
                  x = "Value [million DKK]",
                  y = "Density") +
             theme_minimal()
}

# -------------------------
```

## 4.7 Standard-house sensitivty
The code below examines how sensitive the lot-value estimates are to the choice of standard house. Several alternative specifications are considered by varying the reference dwelling’s living area and construction year while keeping the remaining building characteristics fixed.

For each specification, the lot-sale and property data are standardized to the chosen reference house, and the fold-specific property models are used to calculate corresponding standard-property values. The original lot characteristics are then restored for the lot sales so that only the assumed building characteristics differ across specifications.

The standard-property and combined lot models are subsequently re-estimated for every cross-validation fold under each alternative specification. The resulting model ensembles and standardized datasets are stored together, allowing the estimated lot values, model effects, and predictive performance to be compared across different choices of standard-house parameters.

```{r Sensitivity to standard house parameters, eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE}

# -------------------------
# Sensitivity analysis: standard-house specification
# -------------------------

# -------------------------
# 1. Settings
# -------------------------

sensitivity_dir <- "saved_files/standard_house_sensitivity"

if (!dir.exists(sensitivity_dir)) {dir.create(sensitivity_dir, recursive = TRUE)}

standard_house_specs <- list(
  
  reference_140_1970 = list(year_built = 1970,
                            year_rebuilt = 1970,
                            living_space = 140,
                            lot_size = 800,
                            maximum_coverage_percentage = 30,
                            number_of_divisions = 1,
                            number_of_bathrooms = 1,
                            house_type = "Detached",
                            roof_type = "Fiber cement",
                            wall_type = "Brick",
                            heating_type = "District heating"),
  
  small_100_1970 = list(year_built = 1970,
                        year_rebuilt = 1970,
                        living_space = 100,
                        lot_size = 800,
                        maximum_coverage_percentage = 30,
                        number_of_divisions = 1,
                        number_of_bathrooms = 1,
                        house_type = "Detached",
                        roof_type = "Fiber cement",
                        wall_type = "Brick",
                        heating_type = "District heating"),
  
  large_180_1970 = list(year_built = 1970,
                        year_rebuilt = 1970,
                        living_space = 180,
                        lot_size = 800,
                        maximum_coverage_percentage = 30,
                        number_of_divisions = 1,
                        number_of_bathrooms = 1,
                        house_type = "Detached",
                        roof_type = "Fiber cement",
                        wall_type = "Brick",
                        heating_type = "District heating"),
  
  newer_140_2000 = list(year_built = 2000,
                        year_rebuilt = 2000,
                        living_space = 140,
                        lot_size = 800,
                        maximum_coverage_percentage = 30,
                        number_of_divisions = 1,
                        number_of_bathrooms = 1,
                        house_type = "Detached",
                        roof_type = "Fiber cement",
                        wall_type = "Brick",
                        heating_type = "District heating"),
  
  older_140_1950 = list(year_built = 1950,
                        year_rebuilt = 1970,
                        living_space = 140,
                        lot_size = 800,
                        maximum_coverage_percentage = 30,
                        number_of_divisions = 1,
                        number_of_bathrooms = 1,
                        house_type = "Detached",
                        roof_type = "Fiber cement",
                        wall_type = "Brick",
                        heating_type = "District heating")
  
)

# -------------------------
# 2. Standardization helper
# -------------------------

standardize_property_spec <- function(data, reference_data, spec) {
  
  data %>% mutate(year_built = spec$year_built,
                  year_rebuilt = spec$year_rebuilt,
                  living_space = spec$living_space,
                  lot_size = spec$lot_size,
                  maximum_coverage_percentage = spec$maximum_coverage_percentage,
                  number_of_divisions = spec$number_of_divisions,
                  number_of_bathrooms = spec$number_of_bathrooms,
                  house_type = factor(spec$house_type, levels = levels(factor(reference_data$house_type))),
                  roof_type = factor(spec$roof_type, levels = levels(factor(reference_data$roof_type))),
                  wall_type = factor(spec$wall_type, levels = levels(factor(reference_data$wall_type))),
                  heating_type = factor(spec$heating_type, levels = levels(factor(reference_data$heating_type))))
  
}

restore_lot_variables <- function(standardized_lot_data, original_lot_data) {
  
  standardized_lot_data %>% mutate(lot_size = original_lot_data$lot_size,
                                   maximum_coverage_percentage = original_lot_data$maximum_coverage_percentage,
                                   number_of_divisions = original_lot_data$number_of_divisions)
  
}

prepare_sensitivity_datasets <- function(spec_name,
                                         spec,
                                         property_models,
                                         dataset_lot_sales_cv,
                                         dataset_properties,
                                         reference_data) {
  
  message("Preparing standardized datasets for ", spec_name, " ...")
  
  dataset_lot_sales_cv_standardized_spec <- standardize_property_spec(data = dataset_lot_sales_cv,
                                                                      reference_data = reference_data,
                                                                      spec = spec)
  
  dataset_properties_standardized_spec <- standardize_property_spec(data = dataset_properties,
                                                                    reference_data = reference_data,
                                                                    spec = spec)
  
  for (model_name in names(property_models)) {
    
    dataset_lot_sales_cv_standardized_spec[[paste0("standard_property_value_", model_name)]] <- as.vector(
      predict.gam(property_models[[model_name]], newdata = dataset_lot_sales_cv_standardized_spec, type = "response")
      )
    
    dataset_properties_standardized_spec[[paste0("standard_property_value_", model_name)]] <- as.vector(
      predict.gam(property_models[[model_name]], newdata = dataset_properties_standardized_spec, type = "response")
      )
  }
  
  dataset_lot_sales_cv_standardized_spec <- restore_lot_variables(standardized_lot_data = dataset_lot_sales_cv_standardized_spec,
                                                                  original_lot_data = dataset_lot_sales_cv)
  
  list(lot_sales_standardized = dataset_lot_sales_cv_standardized_spec,
       properties_standardized = dataset_properties_standardized_spec)
  
}

# -------------------------
# 3. Model-fitting helpers
# -------------------------

fit_standard_property_fold_sensitivity <- function(fold, data, k_spatial) {
  
  training_subset <- data %>% filter(validation_set != fold)
  
  standard_property_var <- paste0("standard_property_value_Model", fold)
  
  formula_standard_property <- as.formula(paste0("sales_price ~ ",
                                                 "s(", standard_property_var, ", k = 10) + ",
                                                 "s(lot_size, k = 6, pc = 800) + ",
                                                 "s(maximum_coverage_percentage, k = 3, pc = 30) + ",
                                                 "s(number_of_divisions, k = 3, pc = 1) + ",
                                                 "s(coordinate_east, coordinate_north, k = ", k_spatial,
                                                 ", pc = c(697000, 6150000))"))
  
  bam(formula_standard_property,
      data = training_subset,
      family = tw(link = log),
      method = "fREML")
  
}

fit_combined_fold_sensitivity <- function(fold,
                                          lot_data,
                                          property_data,
                                          k_spatial,
                                          k_other = 10) {
  
  lot_train <- lot_data %>% filter(validation_set != fold)
  
  property_train <- property_data %>% filter(validation_set != fold)
  
  training_subset <- bind_rows(lot_train, property_train)
  
  bam(sales_price ~
      s(coordinate_east, coordinate_north, k = k_spatial, pc = c(697000, 6150000)) +
      s(coordinate_east, coordinate_north, k = k_spatial, by = type_ordered, pc = c(697000, 6150000)) +
      s(sales_date_numeric, k = k_other, by = municipality_type, pc = 2024) +
      s(year_built, k = k_other, by = municipality_type, pc = 1970) +
      s(year_rebuilt, k = k_other, by = municipality_type, pc = 1970) +
      s(living_space, k = k_other, by = municipality_type, pc = 140) +
      s(lot_size, k = k_other, by = municipality_type, pc = 800) +
      s(coast_distance, k = k_other, pc = 1500) +
      s(lake_distance, k = k_other, pc = 500) +
      s(stream_distance, k = k_other, pc = 1000) +
      s(road_distance, k = k_other, pc = 2000) +
      s(highway_distance, k = k_other, pc = 2000) +
      s(train_station_distance, k = k_other, pc = 2000) +
      s(railway_distance, k = k_other, pc = 1000) +
      s(windturbine_distance, k = k_other, pc = 3000) +
      s(ocean_view, k = k_other, pc = 0) +
      s(lake_view, k = k_other, pc = 0) +
      s(forest_size, k = k_other, pc = 0) +
      s(number_of_bathrooms, k = 2, by = municipality_type, pc = 1) +
      house_type * municipality_type +
      roof_type * municipality_type +
      wall_type * municipality_type +
      heating_type * municipality_type +
      type,
      data = training_subset,
      chunk.size = nrow(training_subset),
      family = tw(link = log),
      method = "fREML")
  
}

fit_model_set_sensitivity <- function(fit_fun, N, ...) {
  
  models <- future_lapply(seq_len(N), function(fold) {
    message("Fitting fold ", fold, " ...")
    fit_fun(fold = fold, ...)
  })
  
  names(models) <- paste0("Model", seq_len(N))
  models
}

# -------------------------
# 4. Run sensitivity analysis
# -------------------------

if (load) {
  
  sensitivity_results <- readRDS(file.path(sensitivity_dir, "sensitivity_results.rds"))
  
} else {
  
  sensitivity_results <- imap(standard_house_specs,
                              
    function(spec, spec_name) {
      
      message("Running standard-house sensitivity: ", spec_name)
      
      datasets_spec <- prepare_sensitivity_datasets(spec_name = spec_name,
                                                    spec = spec,
                                                    property_models = models,
                                                    dataset_lot_sales_cv = dataset_lot_sales_cv,
                                                    dataset_properties = dataset_properties,
                                                    reference_data = dataset)
      
      models_standard_property_spec <- fit_model_set_sensitivity(fit_fun = fit_standard_property_fold_sensitivity,
                                                                 N = N,
                                                                 data = datasets_spec$lot_sales_standardized,
                                                                 k_spatial = k_spatial)
      
      models_combined_spec <- fit_model_set_sensitivity(fit_fun = fit_combined_fold_sensitivity,
                                                        N = N,
                                                        lot_data = datasets_spec$lot_sales_standardized,
                                                        property_data = dataset_property_sales_cv,
                                                        k_spatial = k_spatial,
                                                        k_other = k_other)
      
      list(spec = spec,
           datasets = datasets_spec,
           models_standard_property = models_standard_property_spec,
           models_combined = models_combined_spec)
      
    }
  )
  
  saveRDS(sensitivity_results, file.path(sensitivity_dir, "sensitivity_results.rds"))
  
}


```

## 4.8 Illustrative valuations
The code below performs valuations using the combined model framework on a set of simplified, fictitious properties, which are described in the main paper. 

```{r Model interpretation, eval=TRUE, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE}

make_interpretation_results <- function(model, model_name) {
  
  model_data <- model.frame(model)
  
  # generate fictitious properties
  grid <- data.frame(coordinate_east = c(697000, 462037, 469142, 725599),
                     coordinate_north = c(6150000, 6150225, 6322298, 6185920))
  
  point_constraints <- list()
  
  for (sm in model$smooth) {if (!is.null(sm$point.con)) {point_constraints <- c(point_constraints, sm$point.con)}}
  
  vars_in_model <- all.vars(formula(model))
  
  # fill missing variables in grid
  for (var in setdiff(vars_in_model, names(grid))) {
    
    if (is.factor(model_data[[var]])) {
      
      grid[[var]] <- factor(rep(levels(model_data[[var]])[1], nrow(grid)), levels = levels(model_data[[var]]))
      
    } else {
      value <- if (var %in% names(point_constraints)) {
        point_constraints[[var]]
      } else {
        mean(model_data[[var]], na.rm = TRUE)
      }
      grid[[var]] <- rep(value, nrow(grid))
    }
  }
  
  # make lot examples 
  grid$coast_distance[2:4] <- 100
  grid$municipality_type[2:4] <- factor(c("Provincial", "Rural", "Capital"), levels = levels(model_data$municipality_type))
  grid$location <- c("Reference", "Esbjerg", "Nordjylland", "Strandvejen")
  
  #add rows for property case
  grid <- bind_rows(grid, grid)
  grid$year_built[6:8] <- 2020 #place a newer house on the properties
  grid$type[5:8] <- factor("Property sale", levels = levels(model_data$type))
  grid$type_ordered[5:8] <- ordered("Property sale", levels = levels(model_data$type))
  
  terms <- as.data.frame(predict.gam(model, grid, type = "terms"))
  
  # helper for summing possibly missing columns
  sum_terms <- function(df, cols) {
    cols_present <- intersect(cols, names(df))
    if (length(cols_present) == 0) {return(rep(0, nrow(df)))}
    rowSums(df[, cols_present, drop = FALSE])
  }
  
  adjustments <- terms %>%
                 mutate(standard_price = exp(as.vector(coef(model))[1]),
      
                        adjustment_coordinates = exp(`s(coordinate_east,coordinate_north)`),
                        
                        adjustment_type_base = exp(type),
                        
                        adjustment_type_coordinates = exp(`s(coordinate_east,coordinate_north):type_orderedProperty sale`),
      
                        # Smooths with municipality_type interactions – 
                        #might as well sum over all is it only non-zero for the relevant smooth
                         
                        adjustment_sales_date = exp(`s(sales_date_numeric):municipality_typeCapital` +
                                                    `s(sales_date_numeric):municipality_typeRural` +
                                                    `s(sales_date_numeric):municipality_typeCommuter` +
                                                    `s(sales_date_numeric):municipality_typeProvincial` +
                                                    `s(sales_date_numeric):municipality_typeLarge city`),
      
                        adjustment_year_built = exp(`s(year_built):municipality_typeCapital` +
                                                    `s(year_built):municipality_typeRural` +
                                                    `s(year_built):municipality_typeCommuter` +
                                                    `s(year_built):municipality_typeProvincial` +
                                                    `s(year_built):municipality_typeLarge city`),
      
                        adjustment_year_rebuilt = exp(`s(year_rebuilt):municipality_typeCapital` +
                                                      `s(year_rebuilt):municipality_typeRural` +
                                                      `s(year_rebuilt):municipality_typeCommuter` +
                                                      `s(year_rebuilt):municipality_typeProvincial` +
                                                      `s(year_rebuilt):municipality_typeLarge city`),
      
                        adjustment_living_space = exp(`s(living_space):municipality_typeCapital` +
                                                      `s(living_space):municipality_typeRural` +
                                                      `s(living_space):municipality_typeCommuter` +
                                                      `s(living_space):municipality_typeProvincial` +
                                                      `s(living_space):municipality_typeLarge city`),
      
                        adjustment_lot_size = exp(`s(lot_size):municipality_typeCapital` +
                                                  `s(lot_size):municipality_typeRural` +
                                                  `s(lot_size):municipality_typeCommuter` +
                                                  `s(lot_size):municipality_typeProvincial` +
                                                  `s(lot_size):municipality_typeLarge city`),
                                              
                        adjustment_coast_distance = exp(`s(coast_distance)`),
          
                        adjustment_lake_distance = exp(`s(lake_distance)`),
          
                        adjustment_stream_distance = exp(`s(stream_distance)`),
          
                        adjustment_road_distance = exp(`s(road_distance)`),
          
                        adjustment_highway_distance = exp(`s(highway_distance)`),
          
                        adjustment_train_station_distance = exp(`s(train_station_distance)`),
          
                        adjustment_railway_distance = exp(`s(railway_distance)`),
          
                        adjustment_windturbine_distance = exp(`s(windturbine_distance)`),
          
                        adjustment_ocean_view = exp(`s(ocean_view)`),
          
                        adjustment_lake_view = exp(`s(lake_view)`),
          
                        adjustment_forest_size = exp(`s(forest_size)`),
          
                        adjustment_number_of_bathrooms = exp(`s(number_of_bathrooms):municipality_typeCapital` +
                                                             `s(number_of_bathrooms):municipality_typeRural` +
                                                             `s(number_of_bathrooms):municipality_typeCommuter` +
                                                             `s(number_of_bathrooms):municipality_typeProvincial` +
                                                             `s(number_of_bathrooms):municipality_typeLarge city`),
      
                        #Factor terms with interactions
                        adjustment_municipality_type = exp(municipality_type),
                        adjustment_house_type = exp(house_type + `house_type:municipality_type`),
                        adjustment_roof_type = exp(roof_type + `municipality_type:roof_type`),
                        adjustment_wall_type = exp(wall_type + `municipality_type:wall_type`),
                        adjustment_heating_type = exp(heating_type + `municipality_type:heating_type`),
                        

                        adjustment_location = adjustment_coordinates *
                                              adjustment_sales_date *
                                              adjustment_lot_size *
                                              adjustment_coast_distance *
                                              adjustment_lake_distance *
                                              adjustment_stream_distance *
                                              adjustment_road_distance *
                                              adjustment_highway_distance *
                                              adjustment_train_station_distance *
                                              adjustment_railway_distance *
                                              adjustment_windturbine_distance *
                                              adjustment_ocean_view *
                                              adjustment_lake_view *
                                              adjustment_forest_size *
                                              adjustment_municipality_type,
      
                        adjustment_building = adjustment_type_base * 
                                              adjustment_type_coordinates * 
                                              adjustment_year_built *
                                              adjustment_year_rebuilt *
                                              adjustment_living_space *
                                              adjustment_house_type *
                                              adjustment_roof_type *
                                              adjustment_wall_type *
                                              adjustment_heating_type * 
                                              adjustment_number_of_bathrooms,
      
                        adjustment_total = adjustment_location * adjustment_building,
                        
                        predicted_price = standard_price * adjustment_total) %>%
    
                        select(standard_price,
                               adjustment_type_base,
                               adjustment_type_coordinates,
                               adjustment_municipality_type,
                               adjustment_coordinates,
                               adjustment_sales_date,
                               adjustment_year_built,
                               adjustment_year_rebuilt,
                               adjustment_living_space,
                               adjustment_lot_size,
                               adjustment_coast_distance,
                               adjustment_lake_distance,
                               adjustment_stream_distance,
                               adjustment_road_distance,
                               adjustment_highway_distance,
                               adjustment_train_station_distance,
                               adjustment_railway_distance,
                               adjustment_windturbine_distance,
                               adjustment_ocean_view,
                               adjustment_lake_view,
                               adjustment_forest_size,
                               adjustment_number_of_bathrooms,
                               adjustment_house_type,
                               adjustment_roof_type,
                               adjustment_wall_type,
                               adjustment_heating_type,
                               adjustment_location,
                               adjustment_building,
                               adjustment_total,
                               predicted_price)
  
  grid_out <- grid %>% select(coast_distance, year_built, municipality_type, location, type)
  
  bind_cols(grid_out, adjustments) %>% mutate(Model = model_name, .before = 1)
}

results_all_models <- bind_rows(
  lapply(names(models_combined), function(model_name) {
    make_interpretation_results(models_combined[[model_name]], model_name)
  })
)

saveRDS(results_all_models, "saved_files/results_interpretation_combined_models.rds")

```


# 5. Paper III: On the Accuracy of Hedonic Real Estate Models 

## 5.1 Learning curves
The code below fits a list of models to increasing fractions of the training set and assesses their validation MALE. Learning curves for each municipality type are then plotted.

```{r Learning curves, eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, results = 'hide'}
fractions <- c(0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1.0)
folds <- 1:N

model_grid_fraction <- expand.grid(fold = folds, fraction = fractions)

if (load) {
  models_fraction <- readRDS("saved_files/models_fraction.rds")
} else {
  
  models_fraction <- future_lapply(seq_len(nrow(model_grid_fraction)), function(idx) {
    row <- model_grid_fraction[idx, ]
    
    fit_fold(
      i = row$fold,
      data = dataset_property_sales_cv,
      k_spatial = k_spatial,
      k_other = k_other,
      fraction = row$fraction,
      checkpoint_prefix = paste0("fraction_", row$fraction)
    )
  })
  
  names(models_fraction) <- paste0(
    "Model", model_grid_fraction$fold,
    "_", model_grid_fraction$fraction
  )
  
  saveRDS(models_fraction, "saved_files/models_fraction.rds")
}


get_residuals_fraction <- function(models, dataset, grid_df) {
  
  residual_list <- future_lapply(seq_along(models), function(i) {
    
    model_name <- names(models)[i]
    model <- models[[i]]
    row <- grid_df[i, ]
    fold <- row$fold
    frac <- row$fraction
    
    predicted_sales_price <- predict.gam(model, newdata = dataset, type = "response")
    
    tibble(
      sales_price = dataset$sales_price,
      predicted_sales_price = predicted_sales_price,
      residual_sales_price = predicted_sales_price - dataset$sales_price,
      residual_sales_price_percent = (predicted_sales_price - dataset$sales_price) / dataset$sales_price * 100,
      residual_sales_price_log = log(predicted_sales_price) - log(dataset$sales_price),
      validation = dataset$validation_set == fold,
      municipality_type = dataset$municipality_type,
      Model = paste0("Model", fold),
      fraction = frac
    )
  })
  
  bind_rows(residual_list)
}

residual_df_fraction <- get_residuals_fraction(
  models = models_fraction,
  dataset = dataset_property_sales_cv,
  grid_df = model_grid_fraction
)

saveRDS(residual_df_fraction, "saved_files/residual_df_fraction.rds")

performance_fraction <- residual_df_fraction %>%
                        filter(validation) %>%
                        group_by(fraction, municipality_type) %>%
                        summarise(MALE = mean(abs(residual_sales_price_log)),
                                  .groups = "drop")

plot_learning_curves <- ggplot(performance_fraction,
                               aes(x = fraction, 
                                   y = MALE, 
                                   color = municipality_type)) +
                        geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
                        geom_point() +
                        scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
                        labs(x = "Percentage of training set",
                             y = "Validation MALE",
                             color = "Municipality type") +
                        theme_minimal()

saveRDS(plot_learning_curves, "saved_files/plot_learning_curves.rds")
print(plot_learning_curves)

```


## 5.2 Market noise and other models
The code below estimates the market noise based on properties sold twice and compares this to the error obtained using our GAM model as well as an XGboost model. 

```{r Market noise, eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, results = 'hide'}


### Identify double sales and discard those with changes to interior between sales
dataset_sales <- dataset_sales %>%
                 group_by(id) %>%
                 mutate(n = n()) %>%
                 ungroup() %>%
                 arrange(id)

other_sales <- dataset_sales %>% filter(n != 2)
double_sales <- dataset_sales %>% filter(n == 2)

double_sales <- double_sales %>%
                group_by(id) %>%
                filter(year_rebuilt < 2014,
                       n_distinct(living_space) == 1,
                       n_distinct(lot_size) == 1,
                       n_distinct(year_built) == 1,
                       n_distinct(house_type) == 1,
                       n_distinct(number_of_floors) == 1,
                       n_distinct(number_of_rooms) == 1,
                       n_distinct(number_of_bathrooms) == 1,
                       n_distinct(roof_type) == 1,
                       n_distinct(heating_type) == 1,
                       n_distinct(wall_type) == 1) %>%
                ungroup()


### Fit models to other sales and evaluate on double sales

# 1. Indexation model

if (load){

  time_model <- readRDS("saved_files/time_model.rds")

} else{

  time_model <- gam(sales_price ~ 
                    municipality_type + 
                    s(sales_date_numeric, k = k_other, by = municipality_type, pc = 2024),
                    data = other_sales,
                    family = tw(link=log),
                    method = "REML")

  saveRDS(time_model, "saved_files/time_model.rds")

}


#index double sales
time_model_terms <- as.data.frame(predict.gam(time_model, double_sales, type = "terms"))
time_adjustment <- as.vector(rowSums(time_model_terms[, grepl("sales_date_numeric", colnames(time_model_terms)), drop = FALSE]))

double_sales <- double_sales %>% mutate(log_sales_price = log(sales_price),
                                        log_sales_price_indexed = log_sales_price - time_adjustment,
                                        sales_price_indexed = exp(log_sales_price_indexed))

#index other sales
time_model_terms <- as.data.frame(predict.gam(time_model, other_sales, type = "terms"))
time_adjustment <- as.vector(rowSums(time_model_terms[, grepl("sales_date_numeric", colnames(time_model_terms)), drop = FALSE]))
other_sales <- other_sales %>% mutate(log_sales_price = log(sales_price),
                                      log_sales_price_indexed = log_sales_price - time_adjustment,
                                      sales_price_indexed = exp(log_sales_price_indexed))

#calculate lagged values
double_sales_lagged <- double_sales %>%
                       arrange(id, sales_date) %>%
                       group_by(id) %>%
                       mutate(sales_price_diff_indexed_log = log_sales_price_indexed - lag(log_sales_price_indexed),
                              avg_price = (sales_price_indexed + lag(sales_price_indexed)) / 2,
                              sales_date_diff = sales_date_numeric - lag(sales_date_numeric)) %>%
                       ungroup()

# 2. GAM model

if (load){

  gam_model <- readRDS("saved_files/gam_model.rds")

} else{

  gam_model <- bam(sales_price_indexed ~ 
                   s(coordinate_east, coordinate_north, k = k_spatial, pc = c(697000, 6150000)) +
                   s(year_built, k = k_other, by = municipality_type, pc = 1970) +
                   s(year_rebuilt, k = k_other, by = municipality_type, pc = 1970) +
                   s(living_space, k = k_other, by = municipality_type, pc = 140) +
                   s(lot_size, k = k_other, by = municipality_type, pc = 800) +
                   s(coast_distance, k = k_other, pc = 1500) +
                   s(lake_distance, k = k_other, pc = 500) +
                   s(stream_distance, k = k_other, pc = 1000) +
                   s(road_distance, k = k_other, pc = 2000) +
                   s(highway_distance, k = k_other, pc = 2000) +
                   s(train_station_distance, k = k_other, pc = 2000) +
                   s(railway_distance, k = k_other, pc = 1000) +
                   s(windturbine_distance, k = k_other, pc = 3000) +
                   s(ocean_view, k = k_other, pc = 0) +
                   s(lake_view, k = k_other, pc = 0) +
                   s(forest_size, k = k_other, pc = 0) +
                   s(number_of_bathrooms, k = 2, by = municipality_type, pc = 1) +
                   house_type*municipality_type +
                   roof_type*municipality_type +
                   wall_type*municipality_type +
                   heating_type*municipality_type,
                   data = other_sales,
                   family = tw(link=log),
                   method = "fREML")


  saveRDS(gam_model, "saved_files/gam_model.rds")
}

double_sales <- double_sales %>% 
                mutate(predictions_gam = predict.gam(gam_model, double_sales, type = "link"),
                       residuals_gam =  log_sales_price_indexed - predictions_gam)

other_sales <- other_sales %>% 
               mutate(predictions_gam = predict.gam(gam_model, other_sales, type = "link"),
                      residuals_gam =  log_sales_price_indexed - predictions_gam)

# 3. XGboost Models (fitted to log sales prices and GAM residuals)

dummy_model_other <- dummyVars(~ roof_type +
                                 wall_type +
```

### 5.3 Number of folds for model ensemble
The code below fits the model ensemble for numbers of fold for the model ensembles and examines the ensemble spread af a function of this.

```{r Number of folds, eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, results='hide'}
if (load) {
  models_folds <- readRDS("saved_files/models_folds.rds")
  data_folds <- readRDS("saved_files/data_folds.rds")
} else {

  N_values <- c(2,3,4,8)

  data_folds <- lapply(N_values, function(N_current) {assign_cv_folds(dataset_sales, N = N_current, seed = 123)})
  
  names(data_folds) <- paste0("N", N_values)

  models_folds <- lapply(seq_along(N_values), function(j) {
    
    N_current <- N_values[j]
    data_current <- data_folds[[j]]

    models_current <- future_lapply(1:N_current, function(i) {
      
      fit_fold(i = i,
               data = data_current,
               k_spatial = k_spatial,
               k_other = k_other,
               fraction = 1.0,
               checkpoint_prefix = paste0("N", N_current))
      })

    names(models_current) <- paste0("Model", 1:N_current)
    models_current
    
    })
  
  
  names(models_folds) <- paste0("N", N_values)

  saveRDS(models_folds, "saved_files/models_folds.rds")
  saveRDS(data_folds, "saved_files/data_folds.rds")
}

get_ensemble_spread <- function(model_list, dataset, N_value) {

  predictions <- imap(model_list, function(model, name) {
    preds <- predict.gam(model, dataset, type = "link", se.fit = FALSE)
    tibble(!!paste0("pred_", name) := as.vector(preds))
  })

  pred_matrix <- bind_cols(predictions)
  pred_cols <- grep("^pred_", names(pred_matrix), value = TRUE)

  spread_df <- bind_cols(dataset, pred_matrix) %>%
               rowwise() %>%
               mutate(sigma_Ensemble = sd(c_across(all_of(pred_cols)))) %>%
               ungroup() %>%
               mutate(N = N_value)

  spread_df
}

property_spread_folds <- bind_rows(
  lapply(names(models_folds), function(name) {
    N_current <- as.numeric(sub("^N", "", name))
    get_ensemble_spread(
      model_list = models_folds[[name]],
      dataset = dataset_properties,
      N_value = N_current
    )
  })
)

saveRDS(property_spread_folds, "saved_files/property_spread_folds.rds")

spread_summary <- property_spread_folds %>%
                  group_by(N) %>%
                  summarise(q05 = quantile(sigma_Ensemble, 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
                            median = median(sigma_Ensemble, na.rm = TRUE),
                            q95 = quantile(sigma_Ensemble, 0.95, na.rm = TRUE),
                            mean = mean(sigma_Ensemble, na.rm = TRUE),
                            .groups = "drop")

saveRDS(spread_summary, "saved_files/spread_summary_folds.rds")

plot_folds_spread <- ggplot(spread_summary, aes(x = N)) +
                     geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q05, ymax = q95), alpha = 0.2, fill = "grey70") +
                     geom_line(aes(y = median), linewidth = 1) +
                     geom_point(aes(y = median), size = 2) +
                     labs(x = "Number of folds",
                          y = expression(sigma[Ensemble]),
                          title = "Ensemble spread across valuation properties by number of folds")

saveRDS(plot_folds_spread, "saved_files/plot_folds_spread.rds")
print(plot_folds_spread)
```

## 5.4 Interplay between market noise and data scarcity
The code below examines the interplay between and noise and data scarcity by examining the validation MALE in the 2D space of KNN-averaged sales densities and sales prices. 

```{r Interplay, eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, results = 'hide'}

# Parameters
K <- 100 #number of neighbors to average over
N <- 3 #number of clusters in each direction
log_scale <- TRUE #perform partitioning on log scale

# Split data
test_set <- dataset %>% filter(test_set)
training_set <- dataset %>% filter(validation_set != 1, !test_set)

# Predict log price
test_set$sales_price_predicted_log <- as.vector(
  predict.gam(models$Model1, test_set, type = "link")
)

# Find spatial neighbors
neighbors <- knn(
  data = training_set[, c("coordinate_east", "coordinate_north")],
  query = test_set[, c("coordinate_east", "coordinate_north")],
  k = K,
  radius = 0
)

distance_matrix <- neighbors$nn.dists
id_matrix <- neighbors$nn.idx

# Compute local sales densities
test_set$sales_density <- apply(distance_matrix, 1, function(dists) {
  K / (pi * (0.001 * max(dists))^2)
})

# Compute average sales price of neighbors
test_set$avg_sales_price <- vapply(
  1:nrow(test_set),
  function(j) mean(training_set$sales_price[id_matrix[j, ]]),
  numeric(1)
)

# Compute residuals in log space
test_set$resid_sales_price_log <- test_set$sales_price_predicted_log - log(test_set$sales_price)

#Find clusters
price_vec <- if (log_scale) log1p(test_set$avg_sales_price) else test_set$avg_sales_price
density_vec <- if (log_scale) log1p(test_set$sales_density) else test_set$sales_density
price_clusters <- kmeans(price_vec, centers = N)$cluster
density_clusters <- kmeans(density_vec, centers = N)$cluster
price_order <- rank(tapply(test_set$avg_sales_price, price_clusters, mean, na.rm = TRUE))
density_order <- rank(tapply(test_set$sales_density, density_clusters, mean, na.rm = TRUE))

test_set <- test_set %>%
            mutate(price_cluster = price_clusters,
                   density_cluster = density_clusters,
                   price_group = factor(price_order[price_cluster],
                   labels = c("Low price", "Medium price", "High price")),
                   density_group = factor(density_order[density_cluster],
                   labels = c("Low density", "Medium density", "High density")),
                   price_density_label = paste(price_group, density_group, sep = ", "))

plot_clusters <- ggplot(test_set, aes(x = sales_density, 
                                      y = avg_sales_price, 
                                      color = price_density_label, 
                                      shape = municipality_type)) +
                 geom_point(alpha = 0.6, size = 1.5) +
                 scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
                 scale_x_continuous(trans = "log1p") +
                 scale_y_continuous(trans = "log1p") +
                 scale_shape_discrete(name = "Municipality type") +  
                 labs(x = expression("Sales density [sales per km"^2*"]"),
                      y = "Average sales price [DKK]",
                      color = "Cluster") + 
                 theme_minimal()

saveRDS(plot_clusters, "saved_files/plot_clusters.rds")
print(plot_clusters)


#Plot clusters geographically
plot_clusters_geographically <- ggplot() +
                                # Add land/ocean contour
                                geom_contour(data = coordinate_grid,
                                             aes(x = coordinate_east, 
                                                 y = coordinate_north, 
                                                 z = as.numeric(!ocean)),
                                             color = "black", size = 0.4) +
                                # Add price-density group points
                                geom_point(data = test_set,
                                           aes(x = coordinate_east, 
                                               y = coordinate_north, 
                                               color = price_density_label),
                                           size = 0.5, alpha = 0.7) +
                                scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
                                coord_fixed() +
                                theme_void(base_size = 10) +
                                theme(legend.position = "none",
                                      plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
                                      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA))

saveRDS(plot_clusters_geographically, "saved_files/plot_clusters_geographically.rds")
print(plot_clusters_geographically)



#Examine interplay between model performance and clusters
binned_data <- test_set %>%
               filter(!is.na(price_group), !is.na(density_group)) %>%
               group_by(price_group, density_group) %>%
               summarise(count = n(),
                         mean_abs_resid = mean(abs(resid_sales_price_log), na.rm = TRUE),
                         .groups = "drop")

plot_interplay <- ggplot(binned_data, aes(x = density_group, 
                                          y = price_group, 
                                          fill = mean_abs_resid)) +
                  geom_tile(color = "white") +
                  geom_text(aes(label = count), color = "black", size = 3) +
                  scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "MALE") +
                  labs(x = NULL,
                       y = NULL) + 
                  theme_minimal()

saveRDS(plot_interplay, "saved_files/plot_interplay.rds")
print(plot_interplay)

```
